extracted.intended_audience: general literate public; parents, young gentlefolk, and aspiring writers seeking advice on manners, education, conversation, friendship, and poetic composition
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive advice on educating children (balance of mind and body), proper behaviour in dancing and assemblies, the nature and choice of friends, and principles for plain writing and heroic poetry. The material is aimed at guiding social conduct and literary composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced education of children (mind and body)
rubrics_metrics.description: The general Mistake among us in the Educating our Children, is, That in our Daughters we take care of their Persons and neglect their Minds: in our Sons we are so intent upon adorning their Minds, that we wholly neglect their Bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not overlook management of a young Lady's Person, but the Erudition of her Mind is much more to be regarded. Aim to make the Mind and Body improve together; make Gesture follow Thought, and not let Thought be employed upon Gesture. Anti-pattern: educating girls only for ornament produces 'Coquets' and misdirected fancy; educating boys only in mind may leave them physically awkward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness and limits of dancing for breeding
rubrics_metrics.description: So much of Dancing at least as belongs to the Behaviour and an handsome Carriage of the Body, is extreamly useful, if not absolutely necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach enough dancing to secure graceful comportment and ease in company. But excess (all the lessons of a dancing-master without one's own good sense) leads to being an affected fop rather than a well-bred person. Add something of your own to lessons to avoid mere affectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dancing-master's role and its insufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the proper Business of a Dancing-Master to regulate these Matters; tho' I take it to be a just Observation, that unless you add something of your own to what these fine Gentlemen teach you... you will much sooner get the Character of an Affected Fop, than of a Well-bred Man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the dancing-master to learn salutations, carriage, and small rules of good-breeding, but supplement instruction with personal judgment and moral/mental cultivation to avoid mere mannerism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dangers of excessive familiarity in country dancing
rubrics_metrics.description: As for Country Dancing, the great Familiarities between the two Sexes on this Occasion may sometimes produce very dangerous Consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Country dancing may be practised innocently, but be alert to steps and movements that encourage immodesty or familiarity (examples: 'Setting', 'Moll Peatley', 'kissing Dances' where partners linger on lips). Anti-pattern: allowing a daughter to be handled or exhibited in ways that compromise modesty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make gesture follow thought (authentic comportment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The true Art in this Case is, To make the Mind and Body improve together; and if possible, to make Gesture follow Thought, and not let Thought be employed upon Gesture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for natural, sincere behaviour where external grace reflects inner qualities. Avoid training gestures merely for appearance; cultivate the mind so bodily carriage expresses genuine character.

rubrics_metrics.name: First impressions and the value of good carriage
rubrics_metrics.description: We generally form such Ideas of People at first Sight, as we are hardly ever persuaded to lay aside afterwards: For this Reason, a Man would wish to have nothing disagreeable or uncomely in his Approaches, and to be able to enter a Room with a good Grace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn enough of good-breeding and carriage to avoid awkwardness in society (e.g., knowing how to salute, when to stand or sit). Lack of such knowledge produces embarrassment even in learned persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of conversation by company size
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Multitude meet together ... their Debates are taken up chiefly with Forms and general Positions... the most open, instructive, and unreserved Discourse, is that which passes between two Persons who are familiar and intimate Friends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect public assemblies to produce generalities (weather, fashions, news); seek two-person intimate conversations for candid, deep exchange where one may 'discover his most retired Opinions' and test the 'beauty and strength' of sentiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities to seek in a friend
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the several Qualifications of a good Friend, this wise Man has very justly singled out Constancy and Faithfulness as the principal: To these, others have added Virtue, Knowledge, Discretion, Equality in Age and Fortune, and ... a Pleasantness of Temper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer friends who are constant, faithful, virtuous, discreet, reasonably equal in age/fortune, and pleasant-tempered. Also value an evenness of behaviour (æquability); beware of those whose humour swings between amiable and odious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautions about friendship and secrecy
rubrics_metrics.description: If thou wouldst get a Friend, prove him first, and be not hasty to credit him: ... Whoso discovereth Secrets, loseth his Credit, and shall never find a Friend to his Mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test new friends before trusting them; avoid revealing secrets (bewraying secrets is presented as an irrecoverable offence). Anti-patterns: friends who are self-interested, inconstant, upbraid or disclose secrets, or are companions only in prosperity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity of expression as a writing principle
rubrics_metrics.description: I know nothing which more shews the essential and inherent Perfection of Simplicity of Thought... than this, that the first pleases all Kinds of Palates, ... The greatest Modern Criticks have laid it down as a Rule, that an Heroick Poem should be founded upon some important Precept of Morality...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain, simple writing pleases a wide audience (common people and refined readers). Avoid the 'Gothick Manner' or affected epigrammatic style that only a few relish. Measure public success (e.g., Molière's test with an old housekeeper) by whether ordinary readers respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heroic/epic poem composition: moral and national relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: An Heroick Poem should be founded upon some important Precept of Morality, adapted to the Constitution of the Country in which the Poet writes. The next Point ... hath been to celebrate Persons and Actions which do Honour to their Country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose subjects that teach a moral precept relevant to the poet's country and celebrate national-worthy persons/actions. Anti-pattern: selecting remote or irrelevant mythic subjects (examples of criticism: Roman poets choosing non‑Roman heroic subjects were derided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of examples and popular taste to judge works
rubrics_metrics.description: Molière ... could foretel the Success of his Play in the Theatre, from the Reception it met at his Fire-side... The Audience always followed the old Woman, and never failed to laugh in the same Place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test artistic works on ordinary, unpretending audiences as a proxy for broader success; if the common people's reaction is right, refined audiences will follow. Anti-pattern: relying solely on elite or affected tastes to judge general appeal.
